sections.content: *Hol?* (“where?”) asks where someone or something is, and the place answers with *-ban* or *-ben*: *A boltban vagyok.* The vowels of the noun choose. A word with a back vowel takes *-ban* (*bolt* becomes *boltban*), a word with only front vowels takes *-ben* (*kert* becomes *kertben*), and *i* and *í* go along with the other vowels. A final *-a* or *-e* grows long before the ending: *iskola* becomes *iskolában*. A final *-i* stays: *nappali* becomes *nappaliban*.

sections.title: From the place to “in the place”
Who is where
sections.content: The place stands right before the verb. Use *vagyok* for “I”, *vagy* for “you” and *van* for everyone else. *Nincs* says that someone is not there: *Károly nincs az iskolában.* Use *az* before a vowel sound: *az irodában*.

items.spanish: Hol van Anna? Az irodában van.
items.english: Where is Anna? She is in the office.
Károly is not in the school.

sections.content: Only a final *-a* or *-e* changes. A word that ends in a consonant, like *bolt* or *park*, takes the ending as it is. Keep the accent: *irodában* has *á*, and *irodaban* is a misspelling.
